steps.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
In a small shallow bowl, stir together the bread crumbs, cheese, cornmeal, oil, italian seasoning, garlic powder and pepper; set aside.
Coat the rack of a broiling pan with cooking spray. Place the cod on the rack, folding under any thin edges of the filets. Brush with the egg white, then spoon the crumb mixture evenly on top.
Bake in a preheated oven for 10 to 12 minutes or until the fish flakes easily when tested with a fork and is opaque all the way through.

raw_recipe.headline: Cod with Italian Crumb Topping
raw_recipe.description: Baked cod with a parmesan cheese, cornmeal, and italian seasoned crumb topping.

review.reviewBody: After reading several of the reviews for this recipe, we decided to forgo the egg white and replace it with 2T of mayo. mixed w/ 1t. lemon juice. We brused each piece of fish w/ the mixture, followed by the crumb topping. It was delicious! This was an inexpensive, quick and easy meal to prepare.

I read the reviews and made this three ways last night since I had 6 fillets of wild caught Alaskan cod (36 oz). Have to say our family loved these each way and wants this again. A great recipe. I used the breading recipe (double batch) as is but added a salt substitute equal to the garlic powder. I used a knife to stab the fillets to let the flavor penetrate, put them on Al foil with release and added a light olive oil spray. No stick plus easy cleanup. I prepared 4 fillets by rubbing on a very thin layer of mayo . In a separate tray, I put a coating of Old Bay on another filet and Red Lobster Seasoning on the last. I drizzled bottled lemon juice to all and then added the bread crumb mixture to all. For the two seasoned fillets, I drizzled on chardonnay and added some extra to the pan. I baked at 450 but it took 30 minutes to cook (still had very moist fillets). A surprising outcome was that everyone liked the variety. All 3 seasonings had a different taste and each was preferred by different people, but by slight margins. The second time I made these, I used 2 seasonings, the mayo and the Old Bay. This is a great tasting fish recipe.

id change up a few things. I used an egg substitue and added minced fresh garlic and a little salt & pepper. Coated the fish filets with the egg mixture then coated with panko breadcrumbs/parmesan/spice mixture. I added, oregano, thyme, lemon/orange pepper and onion & garlic powder to the panko mixture. Coated the entire filet and cooked them at 400 on a wire rack/broiler pan for about 30 min. It came out perfect and everyone loved it.

Excellent! 
1. made it with mayo and lemon juice instead of egg whites. (Also sauteed some fresh garlic and added that to the mayo).
2. didn't have corn meal so used 1 tbsp of almond flour. 
3. I had thick fillets so after 15 minutes at 450 i cooked for another 15 min at 400. 
4. I added cayyene pepper and hot pepper flakes to the crumb mixture and placed some underneath each filet. 

Felt like a fancy meal. I sauteed some green beans and spinach and added alfredo sauce on the side. Thumbs Up!

Brushed with mayo rather than egg whites, added more spice and melted butter to the panko as suggested. Broiled the crumb topping to brown. Also made a caper based 'tartar sauce' to serve with. It was very good...

Delicious and easy! I also took a reviewer's advice, but instead of brushing w/plain mayo, I brushed it with *wasabi* mayo from Trader Joe's. I also used Italian style bread crumbs and just added a little pepper & garlic powder. I also plucked a few basil leaves from my plant and laid them on top of the mayo, before the crumb mixture. I cooked my 1 lb. fillet for 15 minutes and served it with salad and butternut squash cubes sauteed in butter. YUM! Thank you for the recipe and reviewer suggestions!

This is an excellent recipe- the best fish I've had in years! I followed other reviewers' advice and did not use egg white to coat the fish. Instead, I seasoned the fish with a sprinkle of black pepper and a little lemon juice, and then brushed on a mix of 2 TSP mayo and 1 tsp lemon juice on the fish. I made the breadcrumb mix as directed in the recipe and added it onto the fish after brushing on the mayo and lemon juice mix. We like extra flaky fish, so I cooked it for 25 minutes at 450 in my gas oven. My husband can't get enough of it!

This was delicious. I followed another reviewer's suggestion and substituted lightly seasoned mayonnaise thinned with lemon juice for the egg whites. I used panko bread crumbs and omitted the olive oil. I served with roasted cauliflower and used the leftover crumb topping during the last few minutes of roasting the cauliflower. I will make this many more times!

I made this last night and my 11yo daughter said it was "definitely kid-approved." My partner said it was delicious. My only regret is that it could have used more herbal seasoning. I did sprinkle some fresh cilantro and scallions over mine and that brightened it up. Definitely will make this again.

Love this recipe! The topping adds a nice added crunch. So flavorful! I would recommend seasoning the fish before adding the topping since there is no salt in the topping. I just used salt and pepper and it added flavor. First time I made I used a broiling pan and second time I cover a baking sheet with foil. I loved the foiled pan better. Super easy clean up! Served with lemon wedges.

Delicious! My family loved this! I also followed the review of others and skipped the egg white and used mayo with a tablespoon or so of lemon juice. Kept the fish moist, helped the topping stick to it and added great flavor.
Cod isn't traditionally a flavorful fish but this recipe was tasty. My non-fish eating hubby loved it. I added a kick of spice with some Old Bay and served it with mushroom risotto.
Delicious as is -for the non fish eaters in this house, they liked it very much and I love it!
The only change I would make is I would put down aluminum foil on the pan so it was less to clean up.

I made it exactly as written, and it came out crispy as described. The only thing that it lacked, was seasoning on the fish. The recipe should start off with seasoning the cod filets ahead of the egg wash. But this recipe is for a crispy crust, and that's what you'll get!

It was good. I made a double batch and that was unnecessary. I spread the mixture on top as directed but I think I put to much on. Next time I think using it sparingly and maybe a little less grated cheese or it may have been strong due to doubling the recipe. All in all I will save it. My goal is to find a good recipe for baking cod over always deep fried
